correctness.rationale: The group action t+uC permutes Fourier magnitudes, so orbit reduction is exact. The standalone checker enumerates all 8512 four-point subsets of Z/NZ for N=8,...,17, verifies exactly 122 disjoint affine orbits, encloses each orbit Fourier L1 sum by rational intervals based on exact Machin pi bounds, degree-36 cosine Taylor remainder, and integer square roots, then establishes strict separation of the proposed winner from every other orbit. The checker was run from the current package and exited with the stated success line. Analytic factorization gives all three formulas for the winning values; the complete-bipartite graph ratio is the monotone identity (3) of the primary source. Quantifiers, count conventions, and the finite range match across files.

originality.rationale: The primary October 26, 2026 source explicitly poses global four-point minimizers as Question 9.1 and proves only a strict nonglobal local minimum at N=17 in Proposition 9.2, without claiming the progression global. Its general subgroup equality theorem already covers N=8,12,16 and those are clearly acknowledged. The present exact exhaustive certificate establishes the full global minimum and unique affine minimizing orbit at every N from 8 through 17, including the unproved global assertion at N=17. Other checked mathematical records determine candidate progression norms, support-incidence, or fourth moments, not the global four-subset L1 minimization. Unindexed identical tables remain a risk.

value.rationale: Question 9.1 of the motivating 2026 study isolates the four-element finite Fourier Wiener minimum as the first unsolved small-part case. The cutoff at N=17 is mathematically anchored by that paper’s first strict nonglobal one-exchange local minimum, which makes global certification genuinely necessary. The result determines exactly the first ten sharp values and every minimizing labeling, including distinct odd/progression and even/antipodal mechanisms, and proves global optimality in the prime-order example where local search fails. It is a finite motivated complete classification, not a substituted formula or arbitrary numerical slice.
